key_insight: A universal machine-learning framework can predict spin–orbit-coupled electronic structure across the periodic table, delivering near–ab initio accuracy while being orders of magnitude faster for high‑throughput materials exploration.
problem_solved: Ab initio calculations that include spin–orbit coupling (SOC) are computationally expensive and do not scale for large-scale screening or for diverse chemistries across the periodic table; there was no broadly transferable ML model for SOC-enabled electronic structure.
method: Train a single, physics-aware ML model on spin–orbit-coupled electronic structure data spanning elements across the periodic table.
Incorporate symmetry and relativistic (SOC) effects into the model architecture to capture SOC-driven electronic features and chemical diversity.
Use the trained surrogate to predict SOC-influenced properties (e.g., band structures, splittings) orders of magnitude faster than direct ab initio calculations for high‑throughput screening.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work is a blueprint for building transferable, physics-informed models that replace expensive simulations, enabling large-scale materials discovery and rapid prototyping of quantum materials. It also highlights strategies for integrating domain physics (relativistic effects) into generalizable ML architectures.
